notes: Scope: Delhi (NCT), Jammu & Kashmir (UT) and Ladakh (UT) fully, excluding districts (owned by local-lgd) and the High Court serving them (judiciary-owned, referenced only). Known gaps / unresolved items (flagged confidence=low or noted inline rather than invented): (1) Delhi State Election Commissioner — Wikipedia infobox and body text disagree (Anil Kumar Khachi vs Vijay Kumar Dev); (2) Delhi has no separate Public Service Commission (recruitment via DSSSB/UPSC) so none was created; (3) Delhi State/UT Human Rights Commission — could not confirm existence as a standing body separate from NHRC, so no entity created; (4) LAHDC Leh CEC — Tashi Gyalson's term ended 2025-10-31 and no confirmed successor was found (Ladakh's LAHDC elections are entangled with the 2025-26 statehood/Sixth Schedule agitation); marked vacant/low confidence rather than guessed; (5) J&K Deputy Speaker — could not confirm any officeholder, marked vacant/low confidence; (6) J&K State Election Commissioner B.R. Sharma's cited tenure ends 2025, reappointment unconfirmed; (7) J&K has no State Human Rights Commission (defunct since 2019, superseded by NHRC per J&K High Court ruling, Dec 2020) and no Lokayukta entity was found post-2019 (J&K Accountability Commission predates the UT and could not be confirmed active) — neither was fabricated; (8) Srinagar Municipal Corporation has had no elected council/mayor since its term expired Nov 2023; (9) Ladakh's district count (7, i.e. 5 new districts added in 2026 to the original Leh/Kargil) rests on a single Wikipedia mention and should be re-verified against an official Ladakh UT notification; (10) Individual minister 'since' dates for portfolio allocation (18 Oct 2024 order, J&K) vs swearing-in (16 Oct 2024) are both cited across sources — used swearing-in date for 'since'. All current office-holders were checked against 2025-2026 sources (Wikipedia current revisions fetched 2026-09-25); no WebSearch was available for this run (session search budget was exhausted by sibling segments), so cross-verification relied on WebFetch of Wikipedia pages plus internal consistency checks (e.g. Delhi LG -> Ladakh LG handover corroborated independently on two separate pages). VERIFICATION PASS (2026-09-25, adversarial re-verification): loaded and re-parsed the file; found 0 duplicate IDs, 0 dangling parentId/orgId references, all relation types and entity kinds/sectors/position ranks schema-valid. Re-checked 33 of 37 positions against fresh 2025-2026 sources (Wikipedia current-revision infoboxes/pages via WebFetch and direct curl to the Wikipedia API, since this session's own WebSearch budget was separately exhausted and curl-to-Wikipedia hit the same 429 rate-limit the original agent reported): Delhi LG, Ladakh LG, J&K LG, Delhi CM + all 6 ministers + portfolios, Delhi Speaker/Deputy Speaker/Leader of Opposition, Delhi Chief Secretary, Delhi Police Commissioner, Delhi Assembly seat breakdown, MCD Mayor/Commissioner, NDMC Chairperson, J&K CM + Deputy CM + all 4 ministers + portfolios, J&K Speaker/Leader of Opposition, J&K Chief Secretary, J&K DGP, J&K PSC Chair, J&K Assembly seat breakdown, Jammu Mayor, LAHDC Kargil CEC. All 33 held up as accurate against live sources as of this check; no fabricated or stale facts were found among them (two apparent discrepancies were investigated and resolved IN FAVOUR of the original file: J&K LG Manoj Sinha's since-date is confirmed 2020-08-07 per his own Wikipedia infobox, not 2020-08-06 as a secondary summary suggested; Delhi LoP Atishi's since-date is confirmed 2025-02-23 per her own infobox, not 2025-02-22 as a secondary summary suggested). Left untouched, as-is: the 4 positions already flagged low/medium confidence by the original agent (Delhi SEC Commissioner — name conflict between sources, still unresolved after a further attempt; J&K SEC Commissioner — post-2025 reappointment still unconfirmed; J&K Deputy Speaker and LAHDC Leh CEC — still vacant/unconfirmed) since no additional source could resolve them and inventing a holder is explicitly disallowed. One enhancement made: added a sourced since-date (2022-10-22) to the previously date-less Jammu Mayor holder. One coverage gap noted, not fabricated: Delhi Cantonment Board (a third Delhi local body besides MCD/NDMC) is not represented as an entity here — it is a cantonment board, not a municipal_corporation, so arguably out of the 'every municipal corporation' instruction, but flagging for the merge step to confirm.

entities.name: Delhi (National Capital Territory of Delhi)
entities.description: A union territory with a partial state legislature; the seat of the Government of India. Administered jointly by an elected Legislative Assembly/Council of Ministers (with subjects other than police, public order and land) and a Lieutenant Governor representing the Union.
entities.legalBasis: Article 239AA of the Constitution; Government of National Capital Territory of Delhi Act, 1991

entities.name: Government of the National Capital Territory of Delhi
entities.description: The executive government of Delhi: the Lieutenant Governor (Union appointee) and the elected Council of Ministers headed by the Chief Minister, operating under Article 239AA.

entities.name: Delhi Council of Ministers
entities.description: The Chief Minister and cabinet ministers of Delhi, collectively responsible to the Delhi Legislative Assembly, currently 7-member (CM + 6 ministers) under the Rekha Gupta ministry sworn in 20 February 2025.

entities.name: Delhi Legislative Assembly
entities.description: The unicameral 70-seat elected legislature of Delhi. The 8th Assembly was elected in February 2025; BJP holds 48 seats and AAP 22.

entities.name: Municipal Corporation of Delhi
entities.description: The unified municipal corporation covering most of Delhi (re-unified in 2022 from three prior corporations), providing civic services such as sanitation, primary education and local roads. 250 elected wards + 10 nominated members.

entities.name: New Delhi Municipal Council
entities.description: Civic body for the Lutyens' New Delhi area (government/diplomatic core); unlike MCD it is a nominated body, not elected — chairperson and most members appointed by the Union Government, with the Delhi CM and some MLAs/MPs as ex-officio members.

entities.name: State Election Commission, Delhi
entities.description: Constitutional authority under Article 243ZA/GNCTD Act responsible for conducting elections to the Municipal Corporation of Delhi.

entities.name: Lokayukta of Delhi
entities.description: Anti-corruption ombudsman for Delhi government functionaries. The post has been vacant since the last Lokayukta's term ended around 2020.

entities.name: Jammu and Kashmir
entities.description: A union territory with its own elected legislature, formed on 31 October 2019 from the reorganisation of the former State of Jammu and Kashmir. The Lieutenant Governor retains control of police, public order and All India Services; the elected government handles other subjects. Statehood restoration has been promised but not yet enacted as of September 2026.
entities.legalBasis: Jammu and Kashmir Reorganisation Act, 2019; Article 239A

entities.name: Government of Jammu and Kashmir
entities.description: Executive government of the UT of Jammu and Kashmir: Lieutenant Governor plus the elected Council of Ministers headed by the Chief Minister, restored after the October 2024 Assembly election.
entities.legalBasis: Jammu and Kashmir Reorganisation Act, 2019, Section 55

entities.name: Jammu and Kashmir Council of Ministers
entities.description: The Second Omar Abdullah ministry: Chief Minister, one Deputy Chief Minister and four cabinet ministers, sworn in 16 October 2024, collectively responsible to the J&K Legislative Assembly.

entities.name: Jammu and Kashmir Legislative Assembly
entities.description: Unicameral 90-seat elected assembly (plus up to 5 members nominated by the LG under the 2023 amendment: representation for Kashmiri migrants and displaced persons from Pakistan-occupied Jammu and Kashmir). Elected October 2024 after a decade without an assembly government; the Legislative Council was abolished in 2019.

entities.name: Jammu and Kashmir Legislative Council (abolished)
entities.description: Former upper house of the erstwhile State of Jammu and Kashmir; formally abolished on 31 October 2019 under Section 57 of the J&K Reorganisation Act, 2019. Included here for completeness — the UT legislature is now unicameral.

entities.name: Srinagar Municipal Corporation
entities.description: Municipal corporation for Srinagar city, 74 wards. The elected council's term expired in November 2023 and fresh elections had not been held as of the latest available sources; currently under administrator/caretaker arrangement.
entities.legalBasis: Jammu and Kashmir Municipal Corporation Act, 2000

entities.name: Jammu Municipal Corporation
entities.description: Municipal corporation for Jammu city, 75 wards.
entities.legalBasis: Jammu and Kashmir Municipal Corporation Act, 2000

entities.name: State Election Commission, Jammu and Kashmir
entities.description: Constitutional body conducting elections to Panchayats and Municipalities in J&K.

entities.name: Jammu and Kashmir Public Service Commission
entities.description: Recruits to civil services and gazetted posts of the J&K government.

entities.name: Ladakh
entities.description: A union territory without a legislature, formed on 31 October 2019 from the bifurcation of the former State of Jammu and Kashmir. Administered directly by a Lieutenant Governor appointed by the President; local governance is via two Autonomous Hill Development Councils (Leh and Kargil). Subject of an active statehood / Sixth Schedule protection movement through 2025-2026. Districts figure of 7 reflects 5 new districts (Changthang, Drass, Nubra, Sham, Zanskar) reportedly carved out in 2026 in addition to the original Leh and Kargil districts (1979) — recent and should be re-verified against an official notification.
entities.legalBasis: Jammu and Kashmir Reorganisation Act, 2019; Article 239
entities.hq: Leh (Kargil is the other district HQ)

entities.name: Union Territory Administration of Ladakh
entities.description: The administration of Ladakh, headed by the Lieutenant Governor with an Advisor and Deputy Commissioners for Leh and Kargil districts; there is no Council of Ministers or Chief Minister since Ladakh has no legislature.

entities.name: Ladakh Autonomous Hill Development Council, Leh
entities.description: Elected local self-government body for Leh district (30 seats: 26 elected + 4 nominated) with powers over land, agriculture, health and local development, functioning in place of Panchayati Raj institutions.
entities.legalBasis: Ladakh Autonomous Hill Development Councils Act, 1997

entities.name: Ladakh Autonomous Hill Development Council, Kargil
entities.description: Elected local self-government body for Kargil district (30 seats: 26 elected + 4 nominated), 5th council elected October 2023.
entities.legalBasis: Ladakh Autonomous Hill Development Councils Act, 1997
